newsitem.title: USA: U.S. debt futures begin quiet trading barely mixed.
newsitem.headline: U.S. debt futures begin quiet trading barely mixed.

text.p: U.S. debt futures began pit trading barely mixed, with the market seen drifting and guided mainly by technicals as it waits for fresh fundamental incentive.

The only U.S. economic data slated for release Monday is the March U.S. Federal budget at 1300 CDT/1800 GMT. The month's budget deficit was forecast shrinking to $30.7 billion compared with a prior gap of $44.01 billion.
Two key U.S. government officials were speaking Monday. Treasury secretary Robert Rubin began addressing the Corporate Council on Africa summit at 0730 CDT/1230 GMT.
Rubin said he hopes the Federal Reserve Board nominess will be confirmed as soon as possible.
Federal Reserve vice chairman Alice Rivlin was expected to address an Employment Policy Foundation forum at 1215 CDT/1715 GMT.
But brokers said initial order flows Monday were extremely light, with the scanty lineup of important economic data this week seen leaving futures adrift.
"It's a snoozer-fest," said one Treasury bond futures floor broker of dull early activity. "Nobody really cares, to tell the truth...there are not any sellers."
She said that some players had sold near Friday's close, but after seeing no downside followthrough, they covered over the weekend and early Monday.
Some brokers expected Monday's already light trade to thin further as the day progressed and some players left early before the start at sundown of the Jewish Passover holiday.
"It's pretty dead," said another floor broker in June T-bond futures. "We're in a range, call it between 107-28/32 and 108-14/32...for today anyway."
Starting Tuesday, the market also faces more supply that could spice up bland dealings.
